tools.name: use_connection
tools.description: Register or renew a PostgreSQL connection and verify it. Give exactly one credential source: databaseUrl (stored as given), envVar (name of an environment variable of the server process), or envFile with envKey (a .env file and the key inside it). Prefer envVar or envFile so the password never appears in the conversation. Call this before any other tool when no connection is registered for the project.

databaseUrl.description: Literal connection string, postgres://user:password@host:port/database. It is stored in the registry.

envVar.description: Name of an environment variable of the server process that holds the connection string.

envFile.description: Absolute path of a .env file that holds the connection string. Requires envKey.

envKey.description: Key inside envFile that holds the connection string, for example DATABASE_URL.

id.description: Stable id to register under. Defaults to host-port-database.

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: List the registered connections that have not expired. Never returns a password.

tools.name: forget_connection
tools.description: Remove one connection from the registry and close its pool.

connectionId.description: Id of a registered connection; see list_connections.

tools.name: clear_connections
tools.description: Remove every connection from the registry and close every pool.

tools.name: refresh_connection
tools.description: Reopen a registered connection and resolve its credential source again. Use it after the password or the .env file changed, or after the connection dropped.

connectionId.description: Id of a registered connection; see list_connections.

tools.name: list_schemas
tools.description: List the user schemas of the database behind a registered connection.

connectionId.description: Id of a registered connection; see list_connections.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List the tables and views of one schema (default public) of a registered connection.

connectionId.description: Id of a registered connection; see list_connections.

tools.name: describe_table
tools.description: Describe one table or view: columns with types, nullability and defaults, primary key, foreign keys, and indexes.

connectionId.description: Id of a registered connection; see list_connections.

tools.name: search_schema
tools.description: Find tables and columns whose name contains a term (case-insensitive), across every user schema or one schema. Use it in an unfamiliar database to locate where something lives before calling describe_table. Results are capped per kind.

connectionId.description: Id of a registered connection; see list_connections.

term.description: Text to look for in table and column names, case-insensitive. Not blank.

tools.name: query
tools.description: Run one SQL statement inside a read-only transaction. The server refuses any write. Results are capped at the row limit and flagged with truncated when more rows existed. Bind values with $1, $2 and params.

connectionId.description: Id of a registered connection; see list_connections.

sql.description: A single read-only SQL statement. Use $1, $2 for values.

params.description: Values bound to $1, $2, and so on, in order.

maxRows.description: Maximum rows to return. Capped by the server limit.

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Return the execution plan of one SQL statement as JSON, to judge cost and index use before running it. Without analyze the statement is only planned, so even an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE can be explained safely. With analyze the statement really runs and the plan carries measured times; the transaction stays read-only, so a write is still refused.

connectionId.description: Id of a registered connection; see list_connections.

sql.description: A single SQL statement to explain. Use $1, $2 for values.

params.description: Values bound to $1, $2, and so on, in order.

analyze.description: When true the statement really runs and the plan includes measured times. Default false: plan only.

tools.name: execute
tools.description: Run one INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or DDL statement in a transaction. Depending on the server settings this is refused, needs the human to approve it, or runs directly. When the client cannot ask the human, show the human the connection and the exact SQL, get an explicit yes in chat, and only then set confirmedByUser to true.

connectionId.description: Id of a registered connection; see list_connections.

sql.description: A single SQL statement that changes data. Use $1, $2 for values.

params.description: Values bound to $1, $2, and so on, in order.

confirmedByUser.description: Set to true only after the human explicitly approved this exact statement in chat, when the client cannot ask them itself.
